independence.shared_assumptions: The converter and oracle both read the bound receipt and inventory authorities and the same retained bytes. The oracle has separate archive traversal, line splitting, control tokenization, expected stream construction, and TEI traversal code. Exact archive-member and extraction hashes corroborate shared source bytes; P5 is independently checked from the bound local schema.
independence.source_route: The oracle independently traverses each retained ZIP and its receipt inventory, checks every extracted archive member, derives expected physical line and inline-marker streams, then compares them with the corresponding US/Cth TEI branch and P5 schema.

mapping: The one TEI root contains one text/group with separate US and Cth witness texts in that order. Each source archive member remains a distinct front-matter or book division in archive order. Chapter and verse starts own nested chapter divisions and verse paragraphs; physical lines, headings, paragraph and poetry markers, publisher remarks, and blank lines retain line-specific source pointers. Inline USFM controls remain position-specific TEI milestones. A footnote marker opens an attached TEI note; its fr and ft fields are represented by a label and a footnote-text segment, with every source marker and text position retained. Nonempty physical lines without a structural line marker (including lines beginning with an inline control such as \wj) are represented in source order as source-continuation paragraphs under the current book or chapter, with a TEI ptr target link to the preceding verse. Empty lines remain explicit source-line milestones. No US/Cth content is merged, normalized, deduplicated, corrected, or omitted.

marker_policy.inline_controls: Every recognized inline marker, including plus-prefixed forms and source closers, is retained as an ordered TEI marker event. f opens a footnote note; fr begins a footnote reference label; ft begins footnote text; f* is an explicit marker event at the end of that note. Matched formatting and semantic markers remain explicit start/close events instead of imposing scopes that might cross line or verse boundaries.
marker_policy.line_controls: Book metadata and section headings become TEI heads with their exact source marker in @type. c becomes a chapter div; v becomes a verse ab. p, m, q, q1-q3, pi and related content-bearing lines become source-typed ab elements. b and nb remain empty source-marker milestones. rem becomes a note. periph starts a distinct source periphery division. id, ide, h, toc1-toc3, mt and mt1-mt3 remain ordered source heads.
marker_policy.unknown_controls: Fail closed; conversion does not silently drop an unprofiled control or field.
marker_policy.unmarked_lines: A nonempty physical line without an initial USFM control is attached to the active verse as a source-continuation segment. This preserves the retained line boundary and wording.

scope: Genesis, the complete New Testament, Psalms, and selected Old Testament books as enumerated in profile.json; includes each variant's front page and every retained archive member in accounting. This is not a complete Bible.
source_order: Preserve exact ZIP member order within each US and Cth witness. Preserve physical line order within each extracted USFM member.

unresolved.detail: The retained line opens two \wj controls and closes one. The unmatched start is preserved as a milestone; the source is not repaired.
